Subject: Dedicated capacity: HelioCity expected peak & latency constraints

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for taking this. We're trying to finalize the Dedicated proposal and need a short, runnable estimate of tokens/sec and latency headroom so procurement can size the commitment. High level:
- Target feature: multi-turn summarization + retrieval (RAG) for customer support agent.
- Expected peak concurrent users: 200 active sessions during spikes (approx 18:00 PST peak).
- Typical conversation: ~2.5 prompts per session per minute during a spike.
- Typical prompt length: ~160 tokens; expected generated length average: ~420 tokens.
- SLO: 95th percentile inference latency < 350ms for tail-sensitive flows; < 500ms acceptable during bursts with fallback.

Can you send back an illustrated tokens/sec -> GPU count mapping for the model variants we discussed (redwood-7b-quant, redwood-13b-quant, rdx-30b-ffnopt), including recommended headroom percentage and fallback plan? Also attach any assumptions you use (batching, KV cache reuse, avg seq length).

Appreciate it — Samantha
Samantha Ortiz
Head of Product
HelioCity

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: HelioCity expected peak & latency constraints

Hi Samantha —

Thanks for the profile. Quick read of the CSV attached. I'll summarize a working estimate below and attach a simple workbook with the math (tokens_calc_v1.xlsx). Key assumptions up front:
- Model choices: redwood-7b-quant (fastest), redwood-13b-quant (mid), rdx-30b-ffnopt (highest quality).
- Average total tokens per request = prompt (160) + generation (420) = 580 tokens.
- Peak sessions: 200 concurrent users * 2.5 prompts/min = 500 prompts/min = 8.33 requests/sec. Round up for short bursts to 20 req/sec planning scenario (we'll model multiple TPS points below).
- We assume continuous batching with a 10–40ms batching window and 50% KV cache reuse for multi-turn flows.

Preliminary per-model tokens/sec capacity (empirical bench + quantization multipliers):
- redwood-7b-quant: ~3,400 tokens/sec per A100-equivalent GPU
- redwood-13b-quant: ~1,900 tokens/sec per A100-equivalent GPU
- rdx-30b-ffnopt: ~850 tokens/sec per H100-optimized GPU

Using your 580 tokens/request example:
- 10 req/sec => 5,800 tokens/sec
- 20 req/sec => 11,600 tokens/sec (planning burst)
- 40 req/sec => 23,200 tokens/sec (stress)

Rough GPU count (no headroom):
- redwood-7b-quant: 11,600 / 3,400 = 3.4 -> 4 GPUs for 20 req/sec
- redwood-13b-quant: 11,600 / 1,900 = 6.1 -> 7 GPUs
- rdx-30b-ffnopt: 11,600 / 850 = 13.6 -> 14 GPUs

Recommended operational headroom: 35–45% for enterprise spikes (we recommend 40%). After headroom:
- 7 + 40% margin -> 4 * 1.4 ≈ 5.6 -> round to 6 GPUs (7b)
- 7 * 1.4 ≈ 9.8 -> 10 GPUs (13b)
- 14 * 1.4 ≈ 19.6 -> 20 GPUs (30b)

Fallback & latency notes:
- For the 95th <350ms SLO, aim to keep per-request batching latency < 50ms and target application-level concurrency per GPU below 75% of measured capacity. That pushes preferencing to the next model down or automatic fallback to a lower-precision variant (quantized + KV cache friendly) when 95th begins to drift.
- We include automatic routing: host the 13B quant as primary for quality/cost balance, and fall back to 7B quant for bursts where latency must be protected.

I'll loop in Ben for GPU-footprint and Grace for rollout/runbook items. Attaching tokens_calc_v1.xlsx with the above calculations and a simple per-minute simulation.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Internal: HelioCity throughput math + GPU mapping (notes)

Folks — quick internal note and sanity checks on the numbers Jasmine sent. I'm copying the raw calculations so we have them in-thread for procurement/ops.

Assumptions (explicit):
- Peak planning target: 20 req/sec sustained for 10-minute windows, occasional spikes to 40 req/sec for <2 minutes.
- Token mix: 160 prompt / 420 gen = 580 total avg tokens; 95th gen length ~750 tokens (we should simulate tail).
- Measured bench (local, opt-config):
  - A100-80GB (dense fp16 + quant): redwood-7b-quant ~3.4k t/s, redwood-13b-quant ~1.9k t/s
  - H100-80GB (kernel-opt, fused FFN): rdx-30b-ffnopt ~0.85k t/s

Detailed math (20 req/sec):
- tokens/sec = 20 * 580 = 11,600 t/s
- per-GPU usable capacity target = measured_capacity * 0.75 (operational headroom to respect latency)

Per-GPU usable numbers: 7b: 3,400 * 0.75 = 2,550 t/s; 13b: 1,900 * 0.75 = 1,425 t/s; 30b: 850 * 0.75 = 637 t/s

Needed GPUs at 75% utilization (for SLO safety):
- 7b: 11,600 / 2,550 = 4.55 -> 5 GPUs
- 13b: 11,600 / 1,425 = 8.14 -> 9 GPUs
- 30b: 11,600 / 637 = 18.2 -> 19 GPUs

Operational recommendation: purchase an 8-GPU slab for the 13B quant primary + 2-GPU burst pool (7B quant) as a short-term commit. Why:
- 8x GPU primary (13B quant) gives ~11,400 usable t/s at 75% util (1,425 * 8) — aligns with 20 req/sec target with small headroom for tail and batching efficiency.
- Add 2x GPUs with 7B quant to absorb short spikes and keep 95th latency under 350ms by draining tails to faster model.
- This mix reduces cost versus committing to 19 GPUs for 30B while preserving a path to scale to more H100s if HelioCity prioritizes quality later.

Ops items to include in the proposal:
- Canary: 48-hour canary with synthetic spike tests (10/20/40 req/sec profiles).
- Autoscale burst policy: allow 2-GPU warm burst for 5-minute windows; if sustained >10 min, escalate to manual scale.
- Monitoring: 95th token->latency ties and per-route rollout metrics.

I'll label the numbers in the workbook and produce a one-pager for procurement language.

Ben
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Subject: Proposed Dedicated slab & MAP (HelioCity) — tokens/sec mapping included

Hi Samantha / procurement —

Following internal scoping, attached is a concise mutual action plan (MAP) plus the recommended Dedicated slab sizing. High-level recommendation:

1) Recommended initial commit (cost/latency balance):
   - Primary: 8x A100/H100-equivalent GPUs running redwood-13b-quant as the primary serving model.
   - Burst pool: 2x A100-equivalent GPUs running redwood-7b-quant for latency-protecting fallbacks.
   - Expected steady-state capacity at conservative 75% utilization: ~11,400 t/s -> supports ~19.7 req/sec at 580 tokens/request (aligns to 20 req/sec planning).

2) Headroom & SLO strategy:
   - Operational headroom: ~40% buffer above measured utilization for bursts and model tail lengths.
   - Fallback flow: if 95th exceeds 350ms, automatically route to 7B quant; if sustained overload, enable degraded-mode serving (shorter responses or cached summaries).

3) Validation & timeline:
   - Week 1: Provision slab and run 48-hour canary with synthetic traffic (10/20/40 req/sec).
   - Week 2: Customer-driven pilot with real traffic on a small subset of users.
   - Week 3–4: Adjust autoscale thresholds, finalize SLO commit and procurement SOW.

4) Procurement/doc requests:
   - We will provide SOC2 evidence, SLA appendix, and a draft SOW (helicity_commit_terms-draft.pdf attached). Please confirm the preferred contract start date and billing cadence.

Attachments: helicity_commit_terms-draft.pdf, tokens_calc_v1.xlsx
